chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Ubayd ibn Hafs ibn Qurṭ, from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, from Abū ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, when a bird lands on a house and is caught, is it halal or haram for the one who catches it?' He said, 'O Ismāʿīl, whether it is healthy or not.' I said, 'And what is the healthy one (al-ʿāfī)? May I be your ransom.' He said, 'The one that balances its wings, possessing its wings, goes wherever it wishes; it is halal for the one who catches it.'

key_terms.عَافٍ: Healthy (referring to a bird's ability to fly)

ai.seo_question: Is a bird caught inside a house halal to eat according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition for a wild bird caught indoors to be considered halal, emphasizing physical fitness over the manner of capture. He defines the 'healthy' (ʿāfī) bird as one whose wings are balanced and capable of independent flight, distinguishing it from a weakened or captive-bred specimen. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the intrinsic state of the animal's vitality determines its permissibility, rather than merely the method of acquisition.
